sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-17 01:47 UTC; Scope: Daily; Date range: 2026-11-17 through 2026-11-17; Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent infrastructure dominates today's list: the strongest gains cluster around AI office tooling, code review, skill evaluation, browser control, and agent-to-user workflows. The common direction is turning coding agents from isolated chat helpers into tools that can work inside applications with feedback and guardrails.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: Build an extensible Office SDK for editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing, with product surfaces designed for people and AI agents.
sections.why_notable: The day's largest displayed gain; it brings spreadsheet and document-style editing primitives into an extensible SDK explicitly positioned for both people and agents.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: A Go-based AI code-review CLI combining deterministic pipelines with an LLM agent, line-level comments, built-in checks, and OpenAI/Anthropic compatibility.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain; its hybrid design uses deterministic file selection and rule matching around an agent, emphasizing precise reviews over free-form coverage.

sections.title: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
sections.description: A multi-tier framework for validating, deduplicating, and live-evaluating AI agent skills and plugins across quality, security, compatibility, and impact.
sections.why_notable: A strong daily gain for a comparatively small project; the three-tier model separates deterministic checks, overlap analysis, and live task-impact evaluation.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: An MCP server and CLI that let coding agents inspect, debug, automate, and profile a live Chrome browser through Chrome DevTools.
sections.why_notable: It turns a live browser into an agent-accessible debugging and performance surface, and ranked among today's top gainers.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says official support is for Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing; other Chromium browsers are not guaranteed.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders, covering market analysis, charting, economic calendars, screeners, and strategy development.
sections.why_notable: A high daily gain suggests demand for domain-specific agent workflows, here focused on market research and trading tasks.

sections.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
sections.description: AG-UI is an open, lightweight event-stream protocol that connects agents with user-facing apps, carrying typed events for streaming, tools, shared state, and human input.
sections.why_notable: Its stable 1.0 spec and generated TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs position it as a standard transport layer between agent frameworks and application interfaces.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A local browser-based review layer for coding agents, where people annotate plans and artifacts, review diffs, and send feedback back into agent sessions.
sections.why_notable: It makes human review asynchronous across multiple agents and artifacts; its inbox lets agents continue while users respond later.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: A library of Agent Skills designed for the Stitch MCP server, following the Agent Skills open standard for compatibility with several coding agents.
sections.why_notable: The repository reflects a shift from bespoke agent integrations toward reusable, portable skill packages around an MCP-backed design tool.

sections.title: kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill
sections.description: A local video-editing toolset for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools, machine-readable contracts, and an MCP server for cuts, captions, reframing, and export.
sections.why_notable: It applies agent tooling to a concrete media workflow and differentiates itself with local processing and no cloud/API-key requirement, per its description.

sections.title: google-research/paper-orchestra
sections.description: A multi-agent research-writing pipeline that turns ideas and experiment logs into LaTeX manuscripts using literature synthesis, outlining, section writing, refinement, and figure generation.
sections.why_notable: A specific research-authoring application stands out amid general agent infrastructure, with a notable gain relative to its current star base.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the project is not an officially supported Google product and that its generation dataset is not included in this repository.

sections.title: DeanChensj/jiangshan-map
sections.description: An interactive historical atlas of China spanning dynasties, territory snapshots, ancient-city and place-name genealogy, poetry and battlefield landmarks, plus a scrub-through timeline.
sections.why_notable: A non-agent counterpoint in the daily list: a richly scoped interactive historical atlas showing interest in specialized data visualization and cultural projects.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An AI-agent research skill that searches Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket, and the web before synthesizing grounded summaries.
sections.why_notable: A mature research skill remains in the daily list, illustrating that cross-source evidence gathering is becoming a reusable agent capability.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflow infrastructure is the strongest common thread: Open Code Review and SkillEvaluator add review and evaluation controls; Chrome DevTools MCP and AG-UI connect agents to browser and application surfaces; Plannotator returns human feedback into agent sessions. Univer embeds AI in office editing and PaperOrchestra targets research authoring. MCP, event protocols, CLI workflows, portable skills, and local tools recur. TypeScript and Python lead at five repositories each, followed by Go and JavaScript at one each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's leaderboard favors the connective tissue around AI agents more than another standalone model: interfaces, code review, evaluation, browser access, and human feedback loops. The top gainers also include AI-augmented office and research products, while the atlas and trading-skill projects show that specialist applications can still attract sharp one-day attention. Daily star counts are volatile; the useful signal is the cluster of projects turning agents into supervised, tool-using workflows.
